title: Ordinary localization from bifibrant homotopy recognition
statement: Use model categories, weak factorization systems, functorial factorizations, cofibrant and fibrant objects as defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test], simplicial tensors and cotensors as defined in [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor], and the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Enlarge universes so the categories and localizations below exist as ordinary categories. Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category with a compatible simplicial enrichment, tensors and cotensors. Choose functorial trivial fibrations $QX\to X$ with cofibrant sources and functorial trivial cofibrations $X\to RX$ with fibrant targets. Let $\mathcal M^{cf}$ be its full subcategory of cofibrant fibrant objects. Suppose (i) a map between these objects is weak if and only if its vertex class in $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)$ has a two-sided inverse, and (ii) for every fibrant $Y$ the two endpoint maps $Y^{\Delta^1}\to Y$ are trivial fibrations. Here $\pi_0$ is path components of geometric realization, equivalently vertex classes under finite zigzags of simplicial edges. Write $q:\mathcal M\to\mathcal L=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$ for the ordinary category obtained from finite composable strings of ordinary arrows and formal inverses of weak equivalences, modulo the composition, identity and inverse relations. Let $H$ have objects $\mathcal M^{cf}$ and arrows $H(X,Y)=\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)$, with composition induced by enrichment. Inclusion followed by $q$ descends to a functor $H\to\mathcal L$ and is an equivalence. An inverse sends $X$ to $RQX$ and an actual arrow $f$ to $[RQf]$. The comparison with the identity is induced by $X\leftarrow QX\to RQX$. For every arrow $a$ of $\mathcal M$, $q(a)$ is invertible if and only if $a\in W$. Every arrow in $\mathcal L$ between images of bifibrant objects is represented by an actual arrow between those objects.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction; agent-written ordinary prerequisite extracted from original lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus proof Step 14. Finite-string localization, bifibrant component category, functorial replacement comparison and saturation; an ordinary categorical argument, not an infinity-localization claim. No Stacks tag is asserted for this homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: Write $p_X:QX\to X$ and $j_X:X\to RX$ for the chosen natural replacement maps. The left and right classes of a weak factorization system are closed under composition: solve a lifting problem against a composite by first lifting across its first factor and then its second (in the right-class case, solve against the last factor first). Thus $0\to QX\xrightarrow{j_{QX}}RQX$ is a cofibration, and $RQX\to1$ is a fibration by choice of $R$. Hence $RQX$ is bifibrant. If $X$ is already fibrant, $QX\xrightarrow{p_X}X\to1$ is a composite of fibrations, so $QX$ is bifibrant as well. Here we use only the weak factorization system and object definitions in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test].

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-written ordinary prerequisite, proof Step 1; finite-string replacement argument under the stated recognition hypotheses.

proof.text: Naturality gives $p_Y\circ Qf=f\circ p_X$ and $j_{QY}\circ Qf=RQf\circ j_{QX}$. All $p$ and $j$ are weak. Two-out-of-three therefore gives, for every actual arrow $f:X\to Y$, the equivalences $f\in W\Longleftrightarrow Qf\in W\Longleftrightarrow RQf\in W$. This both proves preservation and reflection of weak equivalences by $RQ$ and checks that hypothesis (i) may later be applied to $RQf$, whose endpoints are bifibrant by Step 1. The two-out-of-three axiom is part of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test].

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-written ordinary prerequisite, proof Step 2; finite-string replacement argument under the stated recognition hypotheses.

proof.text: The component sets in the statement do form the arrows of a category $H$. For a fixed vertex in either factor, enriched composition from [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor] sends an edge to an edge, hence sends any finite zigzag of edges to such a zigzag. Changing the two representatives in turn shows that composition is well defined on vertex classes. Its identity and associativity equations descend directly from the enriched identity and associativity equations. This uses the statement's definition of $\pi_0$ by vertex zigzags, and needs no Kan condition on the mapping simplicial sets.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-written ordinary prerequisite, proof Step 3; finite-string replacement argument under the stated recognition hypotheses.

proof.text: Let $X,Y$ be bifibrant and let an edge from $f$ to $g$ in $\operatorname{Map}(X,Y)$ correspond under the cotensor adjunction of [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor] to $h:X\to Y^{\Delta^1}$. Write $e_0,e_1:Y^{\Delta^1}\to Y$ for evaluation and $c:Y\to Y^{\Delta^1}$ for the constant path map, so $e_0h=f$, $e_1h=g$ and $e_0c=e_1c=1_Y$. By hypothesis (ii), both $q(e_i)$ are invertible. The last equations force $q(c)=q(e_0)^{-1}=q(e_1)^{-1}$, hence $q(e_0)=q(e_1)$ and $q(f)=q(g)$. Apply this to each edge, in either direction, of a finite zigzag. Thus $G:H\to\mathcal L$, $G(X)=qX$, $G([f])=q(f)$, is well defined; the functor equations follow from those of $q$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-written ordinary prerequisite, proof Step 4; finite-string replacement argument under the stated recognition hypotheses.

proof.text: Define $S:\mathcal M\to H$ by $S(X)=RQX$ and $S(f)=[RQf]$. Functorial replacement and Step 3 give its functor equations. If $w\in W$, Step 2 and hypothesis (i) make $S(w)$ invertible. Define $F:\mathcal L\to H$ on the finite strings in the statement by sending an ordinary arrow $f$ to $S(f)$ and a formal inverse $w^{-1}$ to $S(w)^{-1}$, and multiplying along each string. The composition and identity relations hold because $S$ is a functor; the two inverse relations hold because these are actual inverses in $H$. This is therefore well defined on the quotient, and $Fq=S$ exactly.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-written ordinary prerequisite, proof Step 5; finite-string replacement argument under the stated recognition hypotheses.

proof.text: For every $X$ put $\alpha_X=q(j_{QX})\circ q(p_X)^{-1}:qX\to q(RQX)=GF(qX)$. Both factors are invertible. The two naturality squares for $p$ and $j$ give $GF(qf)\circ\alpha_X=\alpha_Y\circ qf$ for each actual $f:X\to Y$. For $w\in W$ this equality also gives $GF(qw)^{-1}\circ\alpha_Y=\alpha_X\circ(qw)^{-1}$ by multiplying by the two inverses. Iterating along any finite string proves naturality on every arrow of $\mathcal L$. Thus $\alpha:1_{\mathcal L}\xrightarrow{\sim}GF$ is precisely the comparison induced by $X\leftarrow QX\to RQX$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-written ordinary prerequisite, proof Step 6; finite-string replacement argument under the stated recognition hypotheses.

proof.text: When $X$ is bifibrant, Step 1 makes $QX$ bifibrant, so hypothesis (i) makes both $[p_X]$ and $[j_{QX}]$ invertible in $H$. Set $\beta_X=[j_{QX}]\circ[p_X]^{-1}:X\to RQX=FGX$. For an actual $f:X\to Y$ between bifibrant objects, the two replacement naturality equations give $[RQf]\circ\beta_X=\beta_Y\circ[f]$. Every arrow of $H$ is a vertex class, so this proves $\beta:1_H\xrightarrow{\sim}FG$ natural on all of $H$. Moreover, directly from its formula, $G(\beta_X)=\alpha_{qX}$. No assertion that $Q$ or $R$ is an enriched functor was used.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-written ordinary prerequisite, proof Step 7; finite-string replacement argument under the stated recognition hypotheses.

proof.text: For bifibrant $X,Y$ and any $a:qX\to qY$ in $\mathcal L$, define $h=\beta_Y^{-1}\circ F(a)\circ\beta_X\in H(X,Y)$. Using $G\beta=\alpha$ from Step 7 and naturality from Step 6 gives $G(h)=\alpha_{qY}^{-1}\circ GF(a)\circ\alpha_{qX}=a$, so $G$ is full. If $G(h)=G(k)$, applying $F$ and naturality of $\beta$ gives $h=\beta_Y^{-1}\circ FG(h)\circ\beta_X=\beta_Y^{-1}\circ FG(k)\circ\beta_X=k$, so it is faithful. Every object $qX$ is isomorphic via $\alpha_X$ to $G(RQX)$. Together with the explicit natural isomorphisms of Steps 6-7, this proves that $G$ is an equivalence with inverse $F$, having exactly the object and actual-arrow formulas claimed.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-written ordinary prerequisite, proof Step 8; finite-string replacement argument under the stated recognition hypotheses.

proof.text: If an actual arrow $a$ belongs to $W$, $q(a)$ is invertible by the inverse relation in the definition of $\mathcal L$. Conversely, if $q(a)$ is invertible, applying $F$ makes $[RQa]=F(q(a))$ invertible. Since $RQa$ has bifibrant endpoints, hypothesis (i) gives $RQa\in W$, and Step 2 then gives $a\in W$. This establishes saturation without assuming it for the original category. Finally, for any arrow $u:qX\to qY$ with $X,Y$ bifibrant, fullness in Step 8 supplies $h\in H(X,Y)$ with $G(h)=u$. By definition $h=[f]$ for an actual vertex $f:X\to Y$, so $u=q(f)$, proving the stated representation clause.
